doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Swing as dance music versus listening music
summary: Bird ended dancing; jazz is like twentieth-century classical music, and orchestras rarely play it.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Do you think people look back to like the Swing Era when that was pop music and think well why can’t jazz be popular like it was back then.

Well you see they was dancing on that. See that’s another thing. And Bird and them stopped all of that when they got their turn. That’s why Bird had so much trouble, because when they got to the point where they couldn’t dance on it anymore it was all over. And that’s part of the thing that they had. The music came up, it grew out of people having fun and parties and whatever, but I mean this music here is hard. You’re not going to dance on it so you got to listen. And I equate it just like twentieth century classical music. I mean how many orchestras, many of them program one twentieth century piece a year. And two or three, I mean you’re really doing something. So I mean and eventually the people are going to get to it and it’s going to take a while. You know? And like the composers that I really like I don’t get a chance to hear them unless, you know ‘cause orchestras don’t play them. And not that I don’t like Beethoven and all the rest of the people but I mean I want to hear some of the other stuff too.
A lot of it is about selling tickets, isn’t it?
